title: Stewardship
definition: Stewardship is the faithful management of everything God entrusts to a person for His glory and purposes.
summary: Stewardship recognizes that life, time, gifts, resources, and opportunities belong to God.
christFocus: Jesus teaches His servants to be faithful with what has been entrusted to them until He returns.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Stewardship begins with the confession that everything belongs to God. Life, breath, money, possessions, gifts, influence, time, and opportunities are entrusted by Him.

A steward is not an owner acting independently, but a servant accountable to the Master. Faithfulness matters more than comparison or appearance.

Christian stewardship is shaped by love for God and neighbor. It uses resources to serve, give, build up the Church, care for the vulnerable, and advance the mission of Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people live as owners rather than stewards, spending life mainly on comfort, control, or self-protection. Stewardship matters because everything entrusted by God will one day be accounted for.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Ask what God has placed in your hands and how it can serve His purposes. Practice generosity, wise planning, faithful work, and humble service with what you have been given.
